questions.prompt: Ice nucleation is fundamentally a stochastic time-dependent process. However, models usually do not describe heterogeneous ice nucleation using a single time-dependent description. Why not?
questions.answer: Atmospheric particles have too much variability in their freezing properties, so a single time-dependent description is not adequate.
options: Time dependence is not important for ice nucleation, so it is ignored in models
Atmospheric particles have too much variability in their freezing properties, so a single time-dependent description is not adequate
Even a single time-dependent description is too complex to include in models, so a simpler description is used
Laboratory measurements have been unable to capture time-dependent behavior of ice nucleation

questions.prompt: An increase in INPs causes earlier glaciation of a shallow supercooled cloud. Which radiative consequence is most likely?
questions.answer: The cloud will reflect less solar radiation because the ice crystals have lower scattering efficiency than liquid droplets and it will emit less terrestrial (longwave) radiation because cloud cover is decreased.
options: The cloud will reflect more solar radiation because the ice crystals have higher scattering efficiency than liquid droplets
The cloud will emit more terrestrial (longwave) radiation because cloud depth is increased

The cloud will reflect less solar radiation because the ice crystals have lower scattering efficiency than liquid droplets and it will emit less terrestrial (longwave) radiation because cloud cover is decreased

The cloud will reflect more solar radiation because the ice crystals have higher scattering efficiency than liquid droplets and it will emit more terrestrial (longwave) radiation because cloud cover is increased

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct for mixed-phase clouds? Select all correct statements.
options: Ice nucleation occurs at a higher temperature than homogeneous freezing
The INP concentration increases by orders of magnitude as the temperature decreases below 0°C
Close to the homogeneous freezing temperature, the INP concentration becomes high enough that most droplets freeze
The INP concentration in the atmosphere is so low that most droplets do not freeze by heterogeneous nucleation, even at temperatures well below 0°C

questions.prompt: Which of the following parameterisations have been used in models to describe ice nucleation? Select all correct statements.
options: A function of temperature only, with no link to aerosol properties
A function of the number concentration of aerosol particles larger than a defined diameter, with no link to particle composition
A function of the surface active site density of various aerosol particles measured in the laboratory
Using classical nucleation theory and the nucleation rate coefficient
Using parameterisations of particle to particle chemical diversity incorporating stocahstic functions for the freezing time dependence

questions.prompt: What is the typical maximum measured concentration of INPs in the atmosphere at temperatures of -20°C?
questions.answer: The typical maximum measured concentration of INPs in the atmosphere at temperatures of -20°C is around 0.10 cm⁻³, or 100 L⁻¹.
options: 100 cm⁻³
10 cm⁻³
1 cm⁻³

questions.prompt: What is the value of π (pi)?
questions.answerInfo: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, so it is dimensionless.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are greenhouse gases?
questions.answer: The greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor. Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas.
options: Carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO}_2\))
Methane (\(\mathrm{CH}_4\))
Oxygen (\(\mathrm{O}_2\))
Water vapor (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\))
